title: Six-job Queueable billing chain failing mid-run: 4-stage refactor

stages.scenario: A billing engine chains six Queueable jobs to recalculate invoices across 45,000 accounts. At month-end, job 4 fails with UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW. Jobs 5 and 6 never run, hundreds of accounts are left half-updated, and repairing them means rerunning all six jobs. What is the root cause?

options.text: Month-end jobs contend for the same Account rows, and that lock contention is the defect to remove
options.coachingFeedback: Contention explains why job 4 failed, but month-end locks will recur. The damage comes from what happens after any failure: the chain stops and there is no record of progress to resume from.

options.text: Each job enqueues the next, so one unhandled failure ends the run with no saved progress
options.coachingFeedback: When each job starts its successor, an exception in job 4 means the next enqueue never happens. With no progress tracked in a custom object, the run cannot resume from the last finished account, so partial updates stay stranded.

options.text: Job 4 has no try-catch that retries the failed update before it enqueues the next job
options.coachingFeedback: A catch-and-retry in job 4 might survive one lock timeout, but retrying in the same transaction often fails again, and any other exception still ends the chain with no record of which accounts completed.

stages.scenario: The team will rebuild the six operations. Some steps call external systems, admins want to configure some steps without code, and each step must be retryable without rerunning the others. Which design should the architect use?

options.text: Independent steps behind a Step interface, run by a Queueable processor with a Finalizer for failures
options.coachingFeedback: Separate steps can run, retry, and restart on their own, and a Flow-backed step lets admins own the no-code parts. A Finalizer on the Queueable processor captures every failure without per-step error handling.

options.text: One Batch Apex class that runs all six operations inside each execute() call on chunks of 200 records
options.coachingFeedback: Batch Apex isolates failures per chunk, but all six operations share each chunk's transaction, so one failing operation rolls back the other five and retrying it means rerunning them all.

options.text: Six scheduled Flows, each set to start at a fixed time offset after the one before it
options.coachingFeedback: Fixed offsets assume each step finishes on time. When month-end volume stretches one step, the next starts on incomplete data, and nothing retries a step that failed.

stages.scenario: The step processor passes its sandbox tests. Production runs month-end billing for 45,000 accounts, and the legacy chain is the only path proven at that volume. How should the team cut over?

options.text: Replace the legacy chain in a single weekend deployment after a full regression run in a full sandbox
options.coachingFeedback: A sandbox run cannot reproduce month-end lock contention in production, and a single replacement leaves no proven path to fall back to if the new processor misbehaves mid-cycle.

options.text: Run the step processor and legacy chain on every account for one cycle and compare the results
options.coachingFeedback: Both paths would write the same invoices, doubling DML and lock contention at the busiest point of the month and leaving two competing results on each account.

options.text: Route one account range to the step processor by metadata flag; the legacy chain runs the rest
options.coachingFeedback: A flag on a subset limits exposure to accounts the team can reconcile by hand, and flipping it back returns them to the proven chain without a deployment. The framework's step factories are the natural place to evaluate such a flag.

stages.scenario: After cutover, finance must learn within an hour when any step fails, and support must see which accounts a failed step left unprocessed. What should the team build?

options.text: A scheduled Apex job that queries AsyncApexJob each morning and emails finance any Failed jobs
options.coachingFeedback: A morning check misses the one-hour window, and AsyncApexJob records a job's status and error message, not which accounts that step had left to process.

options.text: A Finalizer per step run that logs outcome and failed record IDs and alerts on errors
options.coachingFeedback: A Finalizer runs after every Queueable execution, including failed ones, so one place covers logging for all error conditions, even in future steps that add no handling of their own. Routing WARN and ERROR logs to an alert channel meets the one-hour need.

options.text: Try-catch blocks inside each step that write caught exceptions and record IDs to a custom log object
options.coachingFeedback: Catch blocks only cover errors each step's author anticipated, and limit exceptions cannot be caught at all. A log object also alerts no one until someone opens it.
